substeps.caption: A loading slide (ours) runs its steel plate out of the working bay to the front: the bay is ~130 mm tall and the indenter waits 7 mm over the sample, too tight for a gripper.
The steel mount from chapter 6 (the wire-EDM slice on steel, polished flush) goes on the plate, in its locating ring.
The slide runs back in and the plate sits on the platen: metal on metal from the slice down to the load cell, nothing soft to compress.
Hands clear: the indenter comes down out of its cylinder and presses the 1 mm-radius ball in, an indent 0.25-1 mm wide. The profilometer waits at the right, clear of the platen.
The indenter lifts well clear; the profilometer's carriage runs in along the crosshead and its pick-up passes under the indenter to the indent.
The stylus traces across the indent, line by line, to map its 3D shape.
It lifts and runs back out to the right, and the indenter goes back to its start.
CORSICA fits a stress-strain curve to that profile by finite elements, in minutes.
The slide runs out and the sample comes off.
The slide runs out and the sample comes off.
